limitations: Civilisation worlds run the Qwen3-0.6B text path of the shared semantic space: every run belongs in a GPU slot (about 12-35 s per simulated day at the development population on the shared GPU; on CPU several minutes per day). With 4 GPU jobs for ~18 agents, slot waits of 30-60 min per job bounded how much of the battery could be re-run in this wave.

Inert subsystems of civilisations (no population activity, no autonomous use): education (learn n=0), employment (labor/jobs/firms), institutions (inst), marketplaces (xchg/market), technology invention (caps/pkg) except when an agent declares a capability; owned by other workstreams (econ/dom) in this wave. O.1 and O.n1 fail until they carry activity.
education_skills (Part 10.2 category 6) is a recorded but pending coupling: the population neither studies nor works in a labour market yet; it is listed in SP-10.2 evidence and not counted.

energy_cost_pricing passes energy cost changes through to prices for NEW rentals only (cloud keeps contracted prices), and at the scarce regime the energy bill per core-hour exceeds the compute price (providers lose money) - a modelling gap of the compute market, not fixed here.

SP-17.1: D, E, G, H and Q have no civilisation measurement (Gate Q has no implementation; G/H need the standard population's 256 adaptive / 8 semantic participants); B.6, C.1, C.5, C.6, C.n1, K.1-K.3, K.6, K.7, K.n1, K.n2 are measured only in their purpose-built worlds. The harness reports each as not_measured and fails the gate.
Chains and the invention experiment use LABELLED SCRIPTED reference agents as roots (feasibility, Part 10.3); every later stage is autonomous.

An in-process World.replay / World.from_blob next to a live world changed the live world's trajectory (both the interrupted 3-day run and its uninterrupted reference diverged from the plain run, while a plain cross-process resume was exact). Verification now runs in child processes; the root cause (process-global state shared between worlds) is not identified - see integration_notes.
integration_notes: KERNEL/A: two worlds built in one process are not independent: in-process World.replay(...) / World.from_blob(...) of a civilisation's snapshot changed the trajectory of the live civilisation in the same process (scratch diagnostic diag_observer.py: variants snap / fromblob / replay / otherworld). crucible.civ now verifies in child processes and runs every counterfactual arm in its own process, but in-process forks (World.fork) used by experimenters may be affected; please find the process-global state (artifact pool, sandbox worker pool, semantic caches, model state) that leaks between worlds.

ECON/DOM: civilisations compose work (needs from work bottlenecks), caps, needs, pkg, labor, jobs, firms, learn, inst, xchg, market; make their population activities live and the civ integration metrics (crucible.civ.integration.subsystems: population_events per subsystem) will count them without civ changes. learn is configured with n=0 and labor with workers=0 because their own populations would be second populations (D-15): they need population activities instead.

ECON: crucible.innovation.reference.ServiceCreator needs crucible.innovation.worlds.FORMAT_SCHEMAS for the format it serves; match.stable and route.tsp (FORMAT_POOL of commerce.worlds.draw) have no schema, so agents cannot declare capabilities for them.
CORE-POP: the development population yields about 2,000-2,500 autonomous sessions per simulated day in a civilisation (6,733 in 3 days) - B.2's 100,000 sessions need the standard profile.

QA: civilisation gate tests read crucible.civ.gates' disk cache ($CRUCIBLE_CIV_CACHE) keyed by the digest of the whole crucible package; official runs on the integration branch recompute everything (hours of GPU slot time: Gate P alone is 1,330 simulated days).
